newsitem.title: USA: A few junk bond issuers to tap corporate debt mart.
newsitem.headline: A few junk bond issuers to tap corporate debt mart.

text.p: Despite an improved tone to the market, Friday's corporate debt calendar featured just a few junk bond offerings; but issuers continued to keep a watchful eye on falling U.S. interest rates.
"It's going to be very quiet for high-grades but we should see some high-yield offerings today," said one syndicate official.
Among the issuers expected to tap the market was Delta Financial Corp, with a $150 million seven-year note deal via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, dealers said.
Price talk on the issue is seen between 325 - 375 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Flemings Cos Inc is slated to bring a $500 million two-part 144a debt offering via Bear Stearns, dealers said.
The deal is expected to include $250 million in seven-year senior subordinated notes and $250 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes, dealers said.
Price talk on the seven-year notes is seen between 400 - 425 basis points over Treasuries, while the 10-year issue is seen pricing at a spread of 450 basis points, they said.

Another $105 million in eight-year 144a notes is seen coming to market from Federal Data Corp via BT Securities, players said. Price talk on the issue is seen at 375 basis points over Treasuries, they said.
So far on Friday, American Communications sold $220 million in 10-year notes to yield 13.25 percent. The deal was incrased from an initial size of $170 million, dealers said.
Turning to the high-grade arena, issuance has slowed despite the improved tone to the market, dealers said.
"Market tone has been very good but we would probably have to see a another significant rally in order to get a lot more issuance," said one syndicate official.

"When we got through 7.0 percent, about a month or two ago, everyone was waiting for that; then we got into the 6.70 percent area and we saw a lot of business get done," he explained. "If we get to 6.25 percent we'll see issuance jump up again.."
The benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury bond is currently yielding 6.53 percent.
Looking ahead, Columbia/HCA Healthcare was expected to issue $200 million in a 31-year debt offering via Salomon Brothers Inc, dealers said.
Unofficial price talk on the A2/A-minus rated deal was seen at 80 basis points over Treasuries, dealer said.
Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc was rumored to be preparing a multi-tranche debt offering for between $600 million to $750 million via Lehman Brothers, dealers said.
FPL Group Inc's Florida Power & Light was also rumored to be ready to tap the market next week with a two-part debt offering, players said.
